en: Vimānavatthu: The Mansion of a Man, Chapter on Pāyāsi The Mansion of a Man, Chapter on Pāyāsi: A Discourse on the Mansion of a Man Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then King Pāyāsi, having risen from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, King Pāyāsi said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I do not believe in the existence of another world, the presence of spontaneously born beings, or the fruit and result of good and evil deeds. When this was said, the Blessed One replied to King Pāyāsi: “Great king, I do not say that there is no other world, nor that there are no spontaneously born beings, nor that there is no fruit and result of good and evil deeds. Then King Pāyāsi addressed the venerable Ānanda: “Venerable Ānanda, I do not believe in the existence of another world, the presence of spontaneously born beings, or the fruit and result of good and evil deeds. The venerable Ānanda replied: “Great king, I do not say that there is no other world, nor that there are no spontaneously born beings, nor that there is no fruit and result of good and evil deeds. A second time and a third time, King Pāyāsi spoke as before, and the venerable Ānanda replied as before. Then King Pāyāsi addressed the venerable Ānanda:

“Venerable Ānanda, I do not believe in the existence of another world, the presence of spontaneously born beings, or the fruit and result of good and evil deeds. Why is that? Because, venerable Ānanda, I have seen here in this very world those who were wealthy, of great fortune, and possessed of vast wealth, yet when they passed away, they were reborn in a state of misery, a bad destination, a state of ruin, or in hell. And I have seen others here who were poor, of little fortune, and possessed of meager wealth, yet when they passed away, they were reborn in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world. Therefore, venerable Ānanda, I do not believe in the existence of another world, the presence of spontaneously born beings, or the fruit and result of good and evil deeds. Then the venerable Ānanda, rising from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and approaching the Blessed One, paid homage to him, stood to one side, and reported all that had occurred to the Blessed One. The Blessed One then addressed the venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, did you hear King Pāyāsi say what he said? “I heard it, venerable sir. “Ānanda, King Pāyāsi has been led astray by four false teachers. For he has been led astray by the false teacher Makkhali Gosāla; he has been led astray by the false teacher Ajita Kesakambalin; he has been led astray by the false teacher Pakudha Kaccāyana; and he has been led astray by the false teacher Sañjaya Belaṭṭhiputta. Ānanda, if King Pāyāsi had been led astray by the false teacher Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, he would have gained faith in the Dhamma. But because he was led astray by these four false teachers, he has become one who does not believe in the existence of another world, the presence of spontaneously born beings, or the fruit and result of good and evil deeds. Ānanda, King Pāyāsi has been led astray by four false teachers. For he has been led astray by the false teacher Makkhali Gosāla; he has been led astray by the false teacher Ajita Kesakambalin; he has been led astray by the false teacher Pakudha Kaccāyana; and he has been led astray by the false teacher Sañjaya Belaṭṭhiputta. Ānanda, if King Pāyāsi had been led astray by the false teacher Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, he would have gained faith in the Dhamma. But because he was led astray by these four false teachers, he has become one who does not believe in the existence of another world, the presence of spontaneously born beings, or the fruit and result of good and evil deeds. Then the venerable Ānanda, rising from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping the right side toward him, and departed. Then the Blessed One, in the evening, arose from meditation and addressed the venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, let us go to the park of King Pāyāsi. “Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied. Then the Blessed One, together with a large assembly of monks, went to the park of King Pāyāsi. At that time, King Pāyāsi was seated in the outer hall with a large retinue of ministers. Then King Pāyāsi saw the Blessed One approaching from afar. Seeing him, he said to his ministers: “Sirs, see how the ascetic Gotama approaches. He is handsome, pleasing, and graceful, possessing a serene countenance, well-restrained, well-composed, with senses calmed, and endowed with supreme mastery over the mind. It is wonderful, sirs, it is marvelous, how the ascetic Gotama, though old, aged, and advanced in years, still possesses such beauty and grace. Sirs, go out and meet the ascetic Gotama, and tell him: ‘Venerable Gotama, please enter the park; the park has been prepared for the venerable Gotama. “Yes, sire,” those ministers replied to King Pāyāsi. They went out to meet the Blessed One and said: “Venerable Gotama, please enter the park; the park has been prepared for the venerable Gotama. The Blessed One consented by silence. Then King Pāyāsi, seeing that the Blessed One had entered the park, rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and approached the Blessed One. Having paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, King Pāyāsi said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Gotama, I do not believe in the existence of another world, the presence of spontaneously born beings, or the fruit and result of good and evil deeds. “Great king, I do not say that there is no other world, nor that there are no spontaneously born beings, nor that there is no fruit and result of good and evil deeds. [The Blessed One then proceeded to describe the various realms of suffering and the heavens, illustrating the truth of karmic retribution through detailed accounts of individuals who, despite their worldly status, experienced the consequences of their actions after death. [King Pāyāsi continued to challenge the Blessed One’s assertions, citing instances where he believed the virtuous suffered and the wicked prospered in this life. [In response, the Blessed One recounted the story of a man who, having committed a grave crime, was reborn in hell, while his friend, who had done nothing wrong, was reborn in heaven, thus demonstrating the infallibility of the law of karma. [The Blessed One further explained the nature of the five aggregates and the process of rebirth, showing how consciousness is conditioned by volitional formations and how beings pass away and reappear according to their deeds. [Finally, the Blessed One described the attainment of the fruits of the spiritual path, from stream-entry to arhatship, and the ultimate goal of nibbāna, which is the cessation of suffering and the end of the cycle of birth and death.

When the Blessed One had finished speaking, King Pāyāsi said this to him: “Venerable Gotama, I now believe in the existence of another world, the presence of spontaneously born beings, and the fruit and result of good and evil deeds. Venerable Gotama, I am like a man who had lost his way and has now found it; I am like a man who was blind and has now regained his sight; I am like a man who was lost in a forest and has now found the path. I take refuge in the Blessed One, the Dhamma, and the Sangha. May the Blessed One accept me as a lay follower who has taken refuge from this day forth for as long as life shall last. “Great king, since you have already been led astray by four false teachers, it will be difficult for you to gain faith in the Dhamma. However, because you have now developed a sense of shame and fear of wrongdoing, you have turned away from unwholesome states and inclined toward wholesome ones. This is a great gain for you, great king. Then King Pāyāsi, having paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping the right side toward him,
2. The Second Mansion of the Householder "Just as the grove of variegated creepers shines forth—
the most excellent garden, the supreme among the Thirty-three gods;"
Just like that, this celestial mansion of yours stands illuminating the sky.
You have attained the power of a deva, O one of great majesty.
"What merit did you perform while being a human being?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing majesty,
and why does your complexion illuminate all directions?"
Thus the son of the gods was delighted...
[as before] ...the fruit of which action this is.
“Both I and my wife, living as householders in the world of men,
with hearts full of faith, [we gave] food and drink.”
We gave abundant gifts with due respect.
Because of that, my complexion is such as this... [and so on].
"And my radiance shines in all directions.
